OPEN-01: Long opening instruction with several tasks. Consider separating spoken identification from report metadata.
BASIS-01: “Outcome” and “in support of it” may be formal. Ask what the person is seeking and why.
BASIS-02: Mixes a question with a record-handling instruction. Keep the instruction out of the spoken question.
DEC-02: Clarify that responsibilities means responsibilities in married life; retain both personal understanding and actual discussion.
DEC-04: “The fact, the discovery and supporting information” is abstract. Clarify what changed, when and how it became known.
CHD-03: “Those expectations” is vague; distinguish a later change from later discovery of an earlier position.
MON-02: “Not disclosed or represented differently” is formal. Consider “not told to you, or described differently.”
MON-05: “Particular fact” needs a clear reference to the financial event being discussed.
PRS-01: Assumes pressure affected the decision. Ask whether there was any pressure first.
PRS-04: “Contemporaneous” is difficult wording; use “information from that time.”
DBT-01: “Serious reservations” could be “serious doubts or concerns.”
WED-01: “Willingness or ability to proceed” is abstract; identify willingness or ability to go ahead with the wedding.
CON-01: “Represented differently or not disclosed” is formal; distinguish a false statement from something not revealed.
CON-05: “Each part of this sequence” needs a clear reference to the events already described.
INF-01: “Unfaithfulness” is vague. Proposed wording uses “affair or adultery”; approval is still required.
INF-02: Keep alleged occurrence separate from discovery; allow unknown dates rather than assuming the event is established.
ABD-04: Combines dates, reasons, uncertainty and support. Ask each component separately if needed.
ABU-01: “Relevant incident or pattern” is vague without naming the reported abuse or behavior.
FTH-01: “Religious affiliation” may be simplified to church or denomination.
FTH-02: “Affiliation or practice” is formal; clarify change of church, faith or religious practice.
BKG-01: “Specific earlier experience directly connected to an issue” is abstract; identify the relevant experience and connection.
BKG-02: Formal wording; ask what happened, how it relates, what was personally known and what was reported.
SEP-02: Assumes living together resumed. First establish whether it did; retain dates and reasons.
SEP-04: “Without treating separation as a new case” is a staff instruction, not an interview question.
REC-03: An instruction rather than a direct question; clarify what the person observed versus was told.
REC-04: “Remains outstanding” is formal; consider “What information is still missing?”
EVD-04: Contains a privacy instruction alongside the question; keep it separate from the spoken question.
MED-03: Contains policy language rather than a follow-up question. Medical wording remains pending review.
